speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I see you've had recent ear pain and trouble wearing earrings after a tympanoplasty. To understand what's happening, can you describe exactly where the shooting pain is located and how long it has been occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: That shooting pain while eating and discomfort with earrings suggests nerve irritation, likely involving the auriculotemporal nerve. Given your history of chronic ear infections and recent surgery, do you notice any swelling, redness, or discharge from the right ear canal?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The pain triggered by eating and discomfort with earrings is highly suggestive of auriculotemporal nerve irritation or entrapment. Do you have any visible swelling, redness, or discharge from the right ear canal currently? Additionally, do you experience any facial weakness or numbness along your jawline or temple?

REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy and Auriculotemporal Nerve Sensory Nerve Action Potential (SNAP) study.
